examples.ko: 전자레인지에 밥을 넣고 이 분 기다렸어요.

I heated up my lunch box in the microwave.

examples.ko: 전자레인지에 우유를 넣고 일 분 돌려요.
examples.en: I put milk in the microwave and run it for one minute.
Do not put aluminum foil in the microwave.

examples.ko: 회사 휴게실에 전자레인지가 있어서 점심을 데워 먹어요.
examples.en: There is a microwave in the office break room, so I heat up my lunch.

explain: 차가운 음식을 따뜻하게 할 때는 ‘데우다’, 물이나 국을 부글부글 끓일 때는 ‘끓이다’를 써요.
explain_en: To warm up cold food, use 데우다. To bring water or soup to a bubbling boil, use 끓이다.

examples.en: After moving, I bought some home appliances.
I looked at refrigerators in an appliance store.
A refrigerator, a washing machine and an air conditioner are all home appliances.

examples.en: When an appliance breaks, I call the service center.

examples.en: What appliances do you need for the new home? — I need a refrigerator and a washing machine.

explain: 컴퓨터와 휴대폰까지 넓게 부를 때는 ‘전자제품’이라고 해요. ‘가전제품’은 줄여서 ‘가전’이라고도 해요.

examples.en: I bought household goods like toilet paper at the mart.
I bought a lot of household items when I moved.
Which floor is the household goods section on?
My friend gave me household goods as a housewarming gift.

examples.en: We've run out of household items. I'm going to buy some this evening.

If you take public transport, you don't have to worry about parking.

examples.en: If you use the dryer, the laundry dries quickly.
Don't put sweaters in the dryer.
Towels fresh out of the dryer are warm and soft.
On rainy days I use the dryer.
I don't have a dryer, so I hang the laundry outside.

explain: ‘건조하다’는 공기나 피부가 메마를 때도 써요: 겨울에는 공기가 건조해요.
explain_en: 건조하다 is also used for dry air or dry skin: 겨울에는 공기가 건조해요 (The air is dry in winter).

examples.en: The lyrics to this song are difficult.
I sing along to the lyrics while I listen.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 가사가 슬퍼서 눈물이 나요.
examples.en: The lyrics of this song are so sad that I tear up.

examples.ko: 노래 가사를 보면 한국어 단어를 배울 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can learn Korean words by reading song lyrics.

examples.ko: 가사는 잘 몰라요. 하지만 노래는 좋아요.
examples.en: I don't really know the lyrics. But I like the song.

explain: ‘가사’는 두 뜻이 있어요. 노래 가사(歌詞)도 ‘가사’이고, 집안일(家事)도 ‘가사’예요. 소리가 같아서 문장으로 구분해요.
explain_en: 가사 has two meanings: song lyrics (歌詞) and housework (家事). They sound the same, so the sentence tells you which one it is.

examples.en: This song has a fast rhythm.
I danced to the rhythm of the music.

examples.ko: 리듬이 좋은 노래를 들으면 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: Listening to a song with a good rhythm makes me feel good.
The drum is an instrument that makes the rhythm.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 리듬이 느려서 잠이 와요.
examples.en: This song's rhythm is slow, so it makes me sleepy.

explain: ‘박자’도 비슷한 말이에요. 노래에서는 ‘박자를 맞추다’(keep time)를 자주 써요.

dict_examples.en: When the music came on, everyone moved to the rhythm.

explain_en: 박자 (beat, time) is a close word. In music you often hear 박자를 맞추다, “to keep time.”
